static_traits.name: Chen Bowen
static_traits.social_status: Has some friends to confide in, but has not yet shared guilt and grief about father with them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems encountered before; has not yet received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good cooperation, able to self-reflect; tending to focus on negative feedback and self-labeling

basic_info.main_problem: I see myself as a bad son for never visiting father, which makes me feel guilty and sad.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing that guilt and grief about not visiting father are affecting my mental health and daily functioning, hence seeking counseling help.
growth_experiences: Moved to a different city for work a few years ago, making regular visits to father difficult; father mentioned feeling lonely and neglected on the phone; the client therefore feels more guilt and gradually avoids answering father's calls to escape the guilt.

Recently experienced a series of unsuccessful dates: obvious anxiety and anticipated failure before dates; feeling inferior and rejected after dates, often repeatedly imagining failure scenarios and focusing on negative feedback.

core_beliefs: I am not liked / not worthy of being liked

special_situations.event: Receives a call from his father or thinks about calling his father
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot visit father often, it means I am a bad son and will make him even lonelier
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding answering calls, reducing contact; finding reasons for not visiting to ease guilt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault,I am a bad son

special_situations.event: When talking with father on the phone, father mentioned feeling lonely and neglected
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If father feels lonely, it is because I have not fulfilled my duty as a son
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Verbally agrees but procrastinates or keeps finding excuses to avoid facing guilt

special_situations.event: Moved to another place for work; hard to visit his father often
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A good son should visit father often; failing to do so equals being unfilial
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-reproach, and trying to justify not visiting with rational interpretation and excuses

special_situations.event: Thinking about the upcoming meeting before a date
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the last few dates went badly, I am doomed to fail again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive worry, rehearsing failure in mind, trying to avoid mistakes through repeated reflection and seeking feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time will also be terrible, I will be rejected

special_situations.event: The other person seeming uninterested during the date
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Her coldness means I am very boring or unattractive
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Post-event rumination focused on negative feedback, ignoring other possible explanations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She finds me very boring / not attractive enough

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be an acknowledged good son, maintaining a close and stable father-son relationship; at the same time longs to be genuinely liked and accepted in intimate relationships
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointing father and being accused of being unfilial; fearing being rejected, seen through and judged in intimate relationships
defense_goal: Through avoiding contact and rationalization, reducing guilt and anxiety, maintaining superficial self-protection

object_relations.object_representation: The father hurt by me, lonely and disappointed

object_relations.self_representation: A suitor who is not liked and easily rejected
object_relations.object_representation: A picky, judgmental potential partner who can 'see through' oneself
object_relations.linking_affect: Shame, anxiety, sense of being rejected

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the topic involves whether to visit her father or answer her father's calls
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client understands others' concern as blame for being 'unfilial', believing one's inaction necessarily hurts father (transference: projection of self-denial)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm but defensive tone, explains work distance and busyness, lists objective obstacles, weakens emotions, and avoids in-depth discussion of guilt.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about dating details, the other party's feelings, or reasons for rejection
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes others will be as picky as past dates, looking down on oneself (transference: projecting inner self-denial onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use uncertain phrasings (e.g. 'they must think...'), hesitant tone, avoid admitting one's own needs, keep distance.

manifestations: Father expressing loneliness and being neglected during calls
The client avoiding contact with father out of guilt, relationship estrangement
Relocated to another place for work; practical conditions limit visiting frequency
Feels tension and a dilemma between autonomous pursuits and family responsibility

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Self-stating 'a good son should visit often', evaluating oneself with 'should/must'
Using whether one visits as the sole standard for measuring self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Turns the original impulse to contact the father into self-blame and guilt
Exerts control over oneself by avoiding answering phone calls rather than communicating directly

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Assuming in dates that the other will look down on oneself, seeing through and judging oneself
Attributing one's insecurity to others' thoughts and attitudes

positive_force: Has some social support (friends to confide in)
Willing to try recording and restructuring thoughts (accepts journaling and alternative-perspective suggestions)
Able to identify and describe negative automatic thoughts (e.g. predicting failure, mind reading)
Having a stable job and life structure
negative_force: Personalizing others' emotions (directly blaming oneself for father's loneliness)
Avoiding contact with father and ruminating, reinforcing guilt
Mental filtering, mind reading and predicting the future, magnifying negative outcomes
Sleep and diet disturbances, impaired functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding contact with father (not answering calls, not visiting)
antecedent: Thinking of calling father or receiving a call from father
Recalling father expressing loneliness and being neglected on calls
Moving away for work, travel inconvenient
target_behavior.core_reason: Directly equating 'cannot visit often' with 'I am a bad son', personally shouldering responsibility for father's loneliness, triggering strong guilt and anxiety, thus reducing discomfort through avoidance
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome emotions (guilt, anxiety) and worries about being judged, relieving psychological pressure in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Father-son relationship further strained, guilt and grief intensified, sleep and diet disrupted, decline in work performance

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive anxiety and negative anticipation before dates (repeatedly imagining failure, mind-reading others)
antecedent: When planning or approaching a date
Recalling and self-ruminating after several unsuccessful dates
target_behavior.core_reason: Based on the core belief 'I am not liked / not attractive enough', making catastrophic future predictions and mind reading, thus anticipating failure
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain a sense of control through rehearsing failure and excessive vigilance, reducing the blow when rejected
target_behavior.consequence: Heightened anxiety, affected performance, worsened self-denial and sense of rejection afterward, further weakening interpersonal and dating experiences
